presentation.title: Maya’s plan
presentation.summary: Let’s focus on the marks first. We’ll simplify your morning layers and introduce one treatment, while keeping the basics your skin already feels comfortable with. You don’t need to replace everything at once.

categoryCards.title: Moisturizer
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I’m keeping this for you

reasons.title: Why I’m keeping this for you
reasons.body: Your CeraVe has felt comfortable for months, and your basic routine sits well under makeup. I’d keep that dependable part of your routine while we introduce the treatment. The pilling shows up on some serum mornings, so removing those extra layers is a better first test than assuming your moisturizer needs replacing.

reasons.title: Optional alternative
reasons.body: When your current bottle runs out, this fragrance-free Water Cream is an option if you’d like to try a different moisturizer. It combines glycerin and hyaluronic acid with ceramide NP and other moisturizing lipids. I’d try it separately once the treatment is settled, and look for comfortable cheeks and good sunscreen and makeup wear. Your CeraVe already works comfortably, so this is a choice, not something you need to buy now.

categoryCards.title: Cleanser
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I chose this for you

reasons.title: Why I chose this for you
reasons.body: Your CeraVe cleanser is comfortable, so I’d finish the bottle first. For your next bottle, I’d try Aveeno Daily Moisturizing Facial Cleanser: $11.60 at Walmart for 12 fl oz, compared with $13.79 at Target for the same size. Both are fragrance-free. Aveeno uses a foaming oat-based formula instead of CeraVe’s creamier wash, but the saving only matters if it leaves your skin just as comfortable.

actions: Finish your current cleanser, and make this switch separately from starting the treatment.
If Aveeno leaves your skin tight or irritated, the lower price isn’t a reason to keep using it.

steps.body: Finish CeraVe first. Avoid switching during the first days of the treatment trial.
Keep your morning water rinse.

categoryCards.title: Makeup removal
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I’m keeping Bioderma for you

reasons.title: Why I’m keeping Bioderma for you
reasons.body: Your Bioderma is already taking your makeup off comfortably, so I’d keep it. There’s no reason to buy a cleansing oil just to add another step. Use a well-soaked soft pad and a light touch, then follow with your cleanser.

reasons.title: Optional alternative
reasons.body: This balm is an option if you’d rather massage makeup off with your fingertips and rinse, instead of using cotton pads. Its oil-rich formula helps loosen makeup, then mixes with water so you can rinse it away. That could make stubborn makeup easier to remove with less repeated wiping. Your Bioderma already works comfortably, so I’d only switch if you prefer this method or find yourself rubbing to get makeup off.

actions: Use it instead of Bioderma, then follow with your regular cleanser. You don’t need both makeup removers.
Look for easy removal without troublesome residue or irritation.

categoryCards.title: Sunscreen
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I’m keeping this for you

reasons.title: Why I’m keeping this for you
reasons.body: Your sunscreen works well with your basic routine. I’d keep it and focus on the serum layering that sometimes makes you use less of it. With the brown marks as our priority, I want sun protection to be the step you can apply properly, rather than the one you cut back to make makeup sit better.

actions: Try the simpler morning routine without the two serums and notice how your usual makeup wears.
Apply generously as directed before going outdoors and reapply at least every 2 hours outdoors. For swimming or sweating, choose a water-resistant sunscreen; this bottle isn’t labeled for that use.

categoryCards.title: Treatments
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I chose this for you

reasons.title: Why I chose this for you
reasons.body: The brown marks that linger after spots are your main concern. Azelaic acid can help reduce the excess pigment behind those marks, which is why I’d choose it over another exfoliating toner. This 10% product gives us an accessible starting option while we learn how your skin tolerates it. The stronger clinical evidence is for 15–20% formulations, so I wouldn’t promise the same results from this bottle. We’ll watch both comfort and gradual change in the marks before deciding what comes next.

actions: Introduce it gradually using the routine guide. Keep the glycolic toner and other new actives out during this trial.
At our check-in, we’ll review application, irritation and the marks together. If progress stalls, we’ll reassess the plan rather than automatically increase the strength.

proposedProduct.name: The Ordinary Azelaic Acid Suspension 10%
proposedProduct.reference: Azelaic Acid Suspension 10% · 30 mL. Follow the manufacturer’s directions.

short.evening: On trial nights only: patch test first and introduce gradually. Follow with moisturizer. Approval does not mean you have started.

instructions: Patch test first, following the manufacturer’s directions. Don’t use the product if the patch test causes redness, burning, itching, blistering or irritation.
After cleansing, let your skin dry. Apply a small amount in a thin layer to intact skin, avoiding eyes, lips and broken skin. Follow with your moisturizer.

First week: try two nonconsecutive evenings. If comfortable, try alternate evenings the next week, then work up to nightly only as tolerated. This is a gradual introduction, not a trial-validated optimal dose.
Keep glycolic toner out and don’t introduce a retinoid or another exfoliant at the same time.
If irritation develops, rinse off and stop. Seek advice if it persists. Get urgent help for swelling or breathing trouble.

categoryCards.title: Your two serums
categoryCards.rationaleTitle: Why I’d pause these for now

reasons.title: Why I’d pause these for now
reasons.body: You’ve been layering these on some mornings without a clear sense of what each adds. I’d pause both while we simplify the routine. Hyaluronic acid and niacinamide can be used together; this is about seeing whether those extra product layers are making sunscreen and makeup harder to wear.

actions: Your moisturizer already provides hydration, so pausing a separate hydrating serum doesn’t mean leaving that need unmet.
If the simpler routine wears better, we can decide whether either serum earns a place back, one at a time.

reasons.title: Why I’d leave this out
reasons.body: You stopped this after your cheeks felt hot and tight, and your basics have felt comfortable again since. I’d leave it out while we introduce azelaic acid. That experience doesn’t mean every ingredient called an acid will behave the same way, but it does tell me we should avoid several new treatments at once.

actions: Don’t push through burning or peeling. Stop the new product if irritation develops and seek advice if it persists.
